news.title: Women's World Cup 2027: Nigeria miss out as South Africa and Ghana win African play-offs
news.lede: Thembi Kgatlana scored two goals at the 2023 Women's World Cup and netted again in Casablanca to keep alive South Africa's hopes of returning to the tournament. Nigeria have failed to qualify for the Fifa Women's World Cup for the first time after the Super Falcons were beaten 2-1 by South Africa in an African play-off at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). Africa's top-ranked team went into the tournament in Morocco as favourites to retain their title but were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Cameroon, having already lost to Malawi in the group stage. With the four semi-finalists guaranteed a spot at next year's World Cup, Justin Madugu's side had one more chance to keep alive their hopes reaching Brazil, with the winner of their one-off tie in Casablanca entering an inter-confederation qualifier.

news.title: ‘This was my World Cup’ says Somali ref after Uefa Super Cup
news.lede: Referee Omar Artan reacts during the Uefa Super Cup match between Paris St-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg, Austria. (EPA Images pic) PARIS: Somali referee Omar Artan described taking charge of Wednesday's Uefa Super Cup between Paris St-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg as his "World Cup". The 34-year-old was denied the chance to referee at the World Cup itself after being refused entry to the United States. He was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport, despite being part of the panel of referees selected by FIFA for the tournament.

news.title: 'Dad rang and I was like: What's happening?' - England U20s boss on Uefa threat
news.lede: Lydia Bedford took up her England role in March. England's head coach Lydia Bedford says she has been told by the Football Association to "just continue as usual" before next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup, despite Uefa threatening to boycott the tournament. Bedford said she had not "thought too much about the bigger picture" as she prepares to name her Young Lionesses squad next week. Football has been engulfed in a major dispute since it emerged that Fifa president Gianni Infantino was planning to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.

news.title: Ghana beats Ivory Coast 2-1 at WAFCON to keep Women's World Cup qualification hopes alive
news.lede: Ghana has come from behind to beat Ivory Coast 2-1 and earn one of Africa’s last two chances to qualify for the Women’s World Cup. Nigeria is to play South Africa for the other later Thursday as the four beaten quarterfinalists at the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations were pitted against each other to decide which two progress to the World Cup intercontinental playoffs. The four semifinalists – Cameroon, Malawi, Morocco and Algeria – have all qualified directly for next year’s tournament in Brazil. Cameroon and tournament debutant Malawi will contest the WAFCON final on Sunday.

news.title: Ghana fight back to beat Côte d’Ivoire and keep World Cup dream alive
news.lede: Ghana came from behind to defeat Côte d’Ivoire 2-1 and secure a place in the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 inter-confederation play-offs after a dramatic TotalEnergies CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations play-off in Casablanca. The Black Queens trailed after just four minutes at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium when Ines Konan converted a penalty to give Côte d’Ivoire the perfect start. But Ghana produced a determined second-half response, with Princess Marfo equalising in the 59th minute before Josephine Bonsu scored from the penalty spot in the 72nd minute to complete the turnaround. The result keeps alive Ghana’s hopes of returning to the Women’s World Cup for the first time since 2007 and gives the Black Queens another route towards qualification for Brazil 2027.

news.title: Rodri transfer news: Man City reject £55m bid from Barcelona for World Cup-winning midfielder
news.lede: Manchester City have rejected a new £55m bid from Barcelona for Rodri. Last week Barcelona had an initial offer in the region of £40m knocked back . On Wednesday, Sky Sports News reported that Barca were expected to raise their offer to between £50m and £60m, but their new offer is still not enough for City. Barcelona remain determined to sign Rodri and are considering their next move.

news.title: The EU has a duty to reform football - LSE European Politics
news.lede: Bridging research, policy and public debate on Europe. High ticket prices at the 2026 FIFA World Cup were heavily criticised by football supporters, but the price of European club football also merits attention. Tsjalle van der Burg argues the EU has failed to apply competition law where it can help football fans most, but special EU sports legislation could help redress the balance. Sky-high ticket prices at this year’s FIFA World Cup sparked much discussion.
